question: In the Fleming's left hand rule index finger indicates the direction of the:
solution:
The correct answer is "**magnetic field**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Fleming's left-hand rule, hold the index finger, middle finger, and thumb of the left hand in **mutually perpendicular directions**.
 
• The** index finger **indicates the** direction of the magnetic field**.
 
• The **middle finger** indicates the **direction of the current**.
 
• The **thumb** indicates the** direction of the force** which results in the motion of the conductor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Magnetic force:**

 
 
• A force called** magnetic force** is produced when electrically charged particles or magnets move.
 
• It is one of the four **fundamental forces** of nature and is a component of the electromagnetic force.
 
• Depending on the magnet's poles or the charge's orientation, it may be **attracted to or repellent.**
 
• Many effects, including electric motors, magnets, compasses, and roller coasters, are caused by it.
 
 
 
• **Electric current:**
 
 
• A flow of particles **(electrons)** moving through wires and other parts is an electric current.
 
• It is the **charge's flow rate**.
 
• A **conductor **is said to have an electric current flowing through it if an electric charge is present.
 
• The flow of charges in circuits using metallic wires is made up of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Motion of Conductor:**
 
 
• A material that easily** permits the flow of electricity** is referred to as an electrical conductor.
 
• Conductivity is the quality of conductors that enables them to **conduct electricity.**
 
• **Electric current** is the name given to the movement of electrons through a conductor.
 
• The **Lorentz force** is experienced by moving charges inside a conductor when there is a magnetic field present that is not parallel to their motion.
